title: Smoothness of a flat group is detected at its identity section
statement:
All group schemes in this statement are schemes [def-pc-scheme] equipped with multiplication, identity and inverse over the indicated base, satisfying the group diagrams (the relative version of [def-sc-group-scheme]). Flatness, smoothness and local finite type have the meanings of [def-weil-flat-morphism, def-sbc-smooth-morphisms, def-weil-finite-type-morphism]. Separated means that the diagonal is a closed immersion [def-weil-closed-immersion]. A Dedekind domain is a Noetherian integrally closed domain of Krull dimension one. Let $S$ be a locally Noetherian scheme and $G\to S$ a flat locally finite type group scheme with identity $e:S\to G$. For each $s\in S$, the morphism $G\to S$ is smooth at every point of $G_s$ if and only if it is smooth at $e(s)$. The subset
$$U=\{s\in S:G\to S\text{ is smooth at }e(s)\}$$
is open, and $G_U\to U$ is smooth. If $S$ is the spectrum of a Dedekind domain and the generic fibre of $G$ is smooth, then $S\setminus U$ is a finite set of closed points. No quasi-compactness, commutativity or Néron mapping property is assumed. Locally Noetherian means that each point has an affine neighbourhood whose coordinate ring satisfies the ascending chain condition on ideals [pqf-def-locnoeth].

proof.text: Write $f:G\to S$. By [pqf-lem-lft-fp-locnoeth], the locally finite type morphism $f$ is locally of finite presentation, since $S$ is locally Noetherian. Put $W=\bigcup\{V\subseteq G:V\text{ is open and }f|_V\text{ is smooth}\}$. Thus $W$ is open and $x\in W$ means exactly that $f$ is smooth at $x$. By [lem-weil-pbc-smooth-local-on-source], applied to this open cover of $W$, $f|_W$ is smooth. The empty union is allowed.

Fix $s\in S$ with $e(s)\in W$ and an arbitrary point $x\in G$ over $s$. Take $K=\kappa(x)$ and its canonical morphism $j_x:\operatorname{Spec}K\to G$ from [lem-weil-pbc-morphism-from-spec-field]. Form $G_K=G\times_{S,fj_x}\operatorname{Spec}K$, with projection $p:G_K\to G$ and structure morphism $f_K$. Its multiplication, unit and inverse are obtained by pulling back those of $G$; the same group diagrams still commute, so it is a $K$-group scheme. The pair $(j_x,\mathrm{id})$ defines a $K$-point $\widetilde x$ of $G_K$ whose image under $p$ is $x$. The base-changed identity $e_K$ maps to $e(s)$. Apply [lem-sfb-scheme-flat-smooth-point-base-change] to $f$ and $\operatorname{Spec}K\to S$: its hypotheses are flatness of $f$ and the local finite presentation obtained in step 1; it imposes no flatness on this change of base. It gives smoothness of $f_K$ at $e_K$.

proof.text: By [def-sc-group-scheme-translate, lem-sc-translation-automorphism], left translation $L_{\widetilde x}$ is a $K$-scheme isomorphism of $G_K$. The unit law gives $L_{\widetilde x}(e_K)=\widetilde x$. If $V$ is an open smooth neighbourhood of $e_K$, then $L_{\widetilde x}(V)$ is an open smooth neighbourhood of $\widetilde x$: its map to $\operatorname{Spec}K$ is identified with $V\to\operatorname{Spec}K$ by this isomorphism. This invariance uses only [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms]: transport each finite presentation through the chart isomorphism, and transport an infinitesimal lifting problem by the inverse isomorphism, lift to $V$, and compose back. Now [lem-sfb-scheme-flat-smooth-point-base-change] at $\widetilde x$ implies that $f$ is smooth at $p(\widetilde x)=x$. Since $x$ was arbitrary, $f$ is smooth at every point of $G_s$. Conversely, that assertion includes the point $e(s)$, proving the equivalence.

source.place: Proof of lemma-group-scheme-field-geometrically-irreducible (translations by rational points); morphisms.tex Tag 02V4 (1). The argument uses the residue field of each point, without a closed-point density argument.

proof.text: The subset in the statement is $U=e^{-1}(W)$, hence is open by continuity of the scheme morphism $e$. Steps 2--3 show $f^{-1}(U)\subseteq W$. Thus $G_U\to U$ is the restriction of the smooth morphism $f|_W$ to the open $f^{-1}(U)$ in its source, with target restricted to $U$. Source restriction preserves smoothness by [lem-weil-pbc-smooth-local-on-source]: use the cover of $W$ consisting of $W$ itself and the specified open. Restricting the target to an open containing the image keeps the same local ring presentations and lifting problems in [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms]. This proves $G_U\to U$ smooth, including the case $U=\varnothing$.

source.place: Tag 01V5, definition-smooth and the following paragraph; Tag 01V6, lemma-smooth-characterize. Openness is the inverse image under the identity section.

proof.text: Finally let $S=\operatorname{Spec}A$ with $A$ Dedekind and let $\eta$ be the prime $(0)$. Apply [lem-sfb-scheme-flat-smooth-point-base-change] to $\operatorname{Spec}\operatorname{Frac}(A)\to S$ at the identity of the generic fibre. The generic-fibre smoothness assumption gives $e(\eta)\in W$, so $\eta\in U$. Therefore $E=S\setminus U$ is closed and avoids $(0)$. Every prime in $E$ is nonzero and hence maximal: a strictly larger prime would give the chain $(0)\subsetneq\mathfrak p\subsetneq\mathfrak q$, contradicting $\dim A=1$. Thus all points of $E$ are closed. Moreover $S$ is Noetherian, having the single affine chart $\operatorname{Spec}A$ with $A$ Noetherian. Apply [lem-sc-noetherian-closed-points-finite] to conclude that $E$ is finite. This finiteness uses the Noetherian affine base, and requires no quasi-compactness of $G$.
